experiment: Full-sweep per-cell decomposition analysis: does overall-accuracy improvement in corrected-trained models (vs standard-trained) reflect genuine balanced discrimination, and is any such effect uniform across early/mid/late swap positions or concentrated in some?
important_ngram_baseline_note: ngram-logreg measured 1.0000 overall / 1.0000 hard-negative accuracy on this task (fix_baseline_ceiling_repeat_01.json) -- it EXCEEDS the theoretical shortcut-only ceiling because alternation validity is a purely local bigram constraint, fully solvable by a bag-of-bigrams model. It is therefore NOT a valid shortcut-only baseline and is NOT used as the exceeds_ceiling_balanced comparison threshold. The threshold is the theoretical ceiling computed from the four structural features (length_parity_even, first_symbol_is_0, last_symbol_is_1, count_balance) only.

criteria.c_exceeds_ceiling_balanced: overall_accuracy > 0.8750 (theoretical shortcut-only ceiling, NOT the ngram-logreg baseline -- see module docstring) AND balanced_any
